newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.AFRICA WATER PARTNERSHIPS MUST BE FAIR - MINISTER.
newsitem.headline: S.AFRICA WATER PARTNERSHIPS MUST BE FAIR - MINISTER.

text.p: Water sector partnerships between government and the private sector must be forged in a climate of competitive bidding and transparency, South African Minister of Water Affairs and Forestry Kader Asmal said.

Releasing on Wednesday his guidelines to local government on the involvement of the private sector in the provision of water services, ahead of proposed water services legislation to be introduced in parliament next year, Asmal said:
"Private sector partnerships in the water sector should be established in an open and transparent fashion and not by stealth."
Three key conditions were given for greater private sector involvement, specifically the handing over of services to private companies for 20 to 30 year long concession contracts.
Asmal said that competitive bidding was essential for the full benefits of private sector involvement to be reaped.
Transparency and full awareness of developments were needed to avoid unnecessary conflict between labour and management and ensure that consumers got the best possible deal, Asmal said.
Finally, he said that coverage was important so that poorer areas were included in more attractive areas, geographically and functionally, to avoid "cherry-picking".
